Training track · 11 stations · 20 levels · 1667 lessons

SF Bay Program Projects — Stormwater, Marsh and Source Control

LIUNA laborers and LIUNA Local 261 shoreline crews, IUOE Local 3 operating engineers, AFSCME and SEIU 1021 public-agency operators and scientists

Programme completion record; each station rehearses the practice its own bodies set — OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P for every cut, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 for any permit space, the MUTCD for work in the street and on the sidewalk, OSHA 1910.120 HAZWOPER inside any contaminated-sediment zone, and the Section 404/401 and BCDC permit conditions for work at the shoreline

The kinds of work the U.S. EPA's San Francisco Bay Program awards of September 2026 pay for — trash capture devices, green stormwater infrastructure, tidal channels and sediment reuse, nutrient reduction at treatment plants, PCB source control and fish habitat — taught as the trade practice each job needs. The stations are generic and sited nowhere real; the Bay Program hub (WebXR/bayprogram/) links each named project to the stations that teach its work.

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Construction & Structural Trades

Bioretention Rain Garden Excavation

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

Green stormwater infrastructure starts as a hole in the sidewalk: the locate ticket matched to the paint, the marked line exposed by vacuum, the cut signalled to grade and the layers placed in the order that makes the cell soak.

  • ANSI/ASSP — ANSI/ISEA 107 — High-visibility safety apparel and accessories
  • union — IUOE local training funds and the IUOE National Training Fund — operating and stationary engineer apprenticeship
  • union — LIUNA Training and Education Fund — construction craft laborer, hazardous waste and environmental remediation curricula
  • MUTCD — Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices — temporary traffic control for work zones (Part 6)
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.21 — Safety training and education in construction
  • OSHA — OSHA 29 CFR 1926.602 Material handling equipment
  • OSHA — OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P Excavations

Street Drain Trash Capture Cleanout

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

A trash capture vault under the street is a permit-required confined space serviced entirely from the surface: the lane closed, the air read at the opening, and the vacuum truck locked out before any hand clears its boom.

  • MUTCD — Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices — temporary traffic control for work zones (Part 6)
  • NIOSH — NIOSH criteria documents, Health Hazard Evaluations and the Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1030 — Bloodborne pathogens
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.146 — Permit-required confined spaces
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.147 — The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
  • RWQCB — Regional Water Quality Control Board Clean Water Act §401 certification and waste discharge requirements

Trash Capture Device Service

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

A large trash capture device only keeps trash out of the Bay while it is serviced, and emptying one means a crane lift with nobody under the bag and nothing shaken back into the channel.

  • union — LIUNA Training and Education Fund — construction craft laborer, hazardous waste and environmental remediation curricula

  • RWQCB — Regional Water Quality Control Board Clean Water Act §401 certification and waste discharge requirements

Tidal Marsh Grading — Amphibious Excavator

13 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

Cutting new tidal channels and lowering berms is heavy equipment on soft ground at the water's edge, worked from the machine with the tide, the permit window and the ground crew all in the operator's picture.

  • BCDC — San Francisco Bay Plan and BCDC permit conditions under the McAteer-Petris Act
  • CDFW — California Department of Fish and Wildlife oversight under the California Fish and Game Code, including Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements (§1602) for work affecting a river, stream or lake
  • union — CWA member training for outside-plant, tower and broadcast work
  • union — IUOE local training funds and the IUOE National Training Fund — operating and stationary engineer apprenticeship
  • union — LIUNA Training and Education Fund — construction craft laborer, hazardous waste and environmental remediation curricula
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926 — Safety and health regulations for construction
  • RWQCB — Regional Water Quality Control Board Clean Water Act §401 certification and waste discharge requirements
  • USACE — Clean Water Act §404 permit conditions for the discharge of dredged or fill material
  • USFWS — Endangered Species Act §7 consultation and species protection measures set by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

Dredge Spoils Dewatering Pad

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

Nutrient Reduction Chemical Feed and Aeration

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

Nutrient reduction at a treatment plant is a chemical feed skid and an aeration basin: the SDS read, the metering pump locked out and bled, the dose calibrated, and the basin read from behind the rail.

  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.132 — Personal protective equipment, general requirements

What it proves

Competency: Clean out a trash capture device, dig a rain garden, work a tidal channel from mats, feed chemicals at a treatment plant, sample a PCB hotspot with chain of custody and keep a fish passage working, each by its own safe procedure

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 11 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 Permit-required confined spaces; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout); OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P Excavations; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.120 Hazardous waste operations and emergency response (HAZWOPER); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 Hazard communication; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 Respiratory protection; US Army Corps of Engineers Clean Water Act Section 404 permit programme; RWQCB Regional Water Quality Control Board Clean Water Act §401 certification and waste discharge requirements; CDFW California Department of Fish and Wildlife oversight under the California Fish and Game Code, including Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements (§1602) for work affecting a river, stream or lake.

These stations also count toward:

  • Confined Space entry, attendance and atmosphere (1 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Respiratory Protection — selection, proving and working on air (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: Programme completion record; each station rehearses the practice its own bodies set — OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P for every cut, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 for any permit space, the MUTCD for work in the street and on the sidewalk, OSHA 1910.120 HAZWOPER inside any contaminated-sediment zone, and the Section 404/401 and BCDC permit conditions for work at the shoreline. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
